nodes.description: Male Cfap58 knockout mice are infertile with severe flagellar defects. A second knockout also showed abnormal manchette structure, misshapen sperm heads and increased sperm apoptosis.
Mice homozygous for an allele mimicking the Pakistani patient stop-gain are infertile with MMAF and sperm axonemes lacking the central pair.

ICSI bypasses the motility defect. One couple from the first replication cohort benefited from ICSI, and a later series reported fertilization and pregnancy with CFAP58-deficient sperm despite profound axonemal defects.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating variants abolish CFAP58 in sperm. CFAP58 lies along the whole flagellum and is concentrated in the midpiece. It has no known enzymatic activity; human sperm studies place it at the connection between radial spokes and doublet microtubules, and mouse studies describe it as a stabilizer of intraflagellar and intramanchette transport cargo such as CCDC42. It is treated here as a structural component of the flagellum.

nodes.description: The 9+2 axoneme is disrupted, the central pair is frequently lost, radial spokes are damaged and accessory structures are disorganized. Central pair (SPAG6) and C1b projection (SPEF2) markers are reduced in sperm. One study of a patient allele in knock-in mice describes a failure of central pair assembly during spermiogenesis; another, in human sperm, places the primary lesion at the radial spoke-doublet interface.
